name: garrow
author: food and the kitchen (kitchen agent)
description:
garrow v6 (direction: food and the kitchen) - A TRAY BAKE, CUT INTO SLICES. PRIVATE; never shown to players.

CLUE = six lines. Lines 1-5 are the uncut tray: a solid crust row of "#", three rows of dough "##::mm::::oo:::pp::::mm::##" (cheese is ":", a two-column crust "##" at each end, every topping a 2-cell piece of a repeated lowercase letter, five pieces a row, at least two cheese cells between pieces, three topping letters drawn from "mpotacsb"), and a closing crust row. The LAST line - after the bottom crust, as in every sibling class - is a CAPTION: the topping letter, a space, a digit, and the word "slice"/"slices" - "m 2 slices". The digit is 0, 2 or 3 (see THE FOOTHOLD; the demo picture v5 insists on needs two counted slices, so 1 is no longer a caption). Trays are 32-38 characters wide and three rows tall. The named topping has 5-7 of the tray's 15 pieces.

ANSWER = the same picture with the knife lines drawn in: a "|" inserted straight down through every row at the same columns. Nothing else may change, so the player's only freedom is where the cuts go; the tray itself is given in the clue, which is what lets a player who has never seen a demo send a well-formed answer.

RULE (unchanged since v1 - every version has changed only what the picture says out loud, and v5 adds only the nought). score = 1 iff (1) the answer, with every "|" deleted, is exactly the clue's dough rows (lines with no ":" - crust rows, the caption, blank lines - are ignored, so the picture is strict but the trimmings are free); and then, if the digit is 0, iff (2a) no row carries a cut at all - the tray is handed back whole; otherwise iff (2b) the cuts are at the same columns in every row, there are at least 4 slices and every slice is at least 3 characters wide, and the number of slices holding TWO OR MORE pieces of the named topping equals the digit - where a piece the knife went through counts for the slice on BOTH sides of the cut. In the picture a halved topping is drawn as "m|m", so "that slice got two mushrooms, and one of them is the half" is readable by eye. One clause a kid says in a breath: "two slices have two mushrooms on them - a mushroom cut in half counts for both sides - and nought slices means don't cut it."

WHAT V6 CHANGES: NOTHING BUT WHERE THE CAPTION SITS. Two Opus players in a row made the same complaint - garrow printed its count on the FIRST line while every other class in the pool prints it last, an inconsistency worth "a parsing bug's worth of attention" and no puzzle value. The caption now follows the bottom crust row, as in basten, durnel, fennick and kelmar. Nothing else moved: the caption text is unchanged ("m 2 slices" / "m 0 slices"), the rule is unchanged, the tray drawn for a given seed is unchanged, and the answer returned for a given tray is byte-for-byte v5's (solve() seeds its search on the clue lines in v5's order, so it picks v5's cutting on every seed). score() takes the caption from the last line and still accepts it on the first, so v5 clues and v5 transcripts still grade; as before it ignores every line without a ":", so the answer is accepted with the caption line kept or dropped. Everything below was re-measured on v6 and is unchanged to the last digit: true rule 100 %, the echoed clue 13.2 % (exactly the nought clues), all 14 well-formedness attacks as recorded. Only the sizes moved (scorer 423 -> 448 chars, solve 4839 -> 4960, generate 8832 -> 8967).

WHAT V5 CHANGES. Picture pool run 5 (lad-durnel-v2-1) scored garrow 26 % for the theorist (one demo) and 0 % for the low-demo player, and both players named the same two faults.

(1) THE FOOTHOLD - "m 0 slices", ANSWER = THE CLUE ECHOED. durnel1a: "garrow has no `0 slices` instances, so unlike its five picture siblings it offers no partial credit at all - an all-or-nothing class." durnel1b had already established the pool-wide convention by probe: "for basten/durnel/fennick, answering the unchanged picture scores exactly when N==0 and never otherwise". garrow was the one picture class where that free check paid nothing. Now ~12 % of clues carry the caption "<letter> 0 slices" (generate() draws the nought on 12.6 % of 20000 seeds, independently of the tray, so a nought tray is drawn from exactly the same distribution as every other), and for those the answer is the tray with the knife left in the drawer. A nought is not a degenerate cutting: an uncut tray is one slice and it holds five to seven of the letter, so "no slice holds two" could never be true of it - the caption is read as "cut it into no slices", and the scorer waives the "at least four slices" clause for that case only. Measured on 500 fresh clues: the echoed clue scores 13.2 %, which is exactly the nought clues and nothing else (with the caption line kept or dropped - both are accepted); every other clue still scores 0 for an uncut answer, because one slice is not four. A player who has only understood the FORMAT banks exactly those clues.

(2) THE DEMO NOW TEACHES THE HALVES CONVENTION. durnel1b, with a demo, read the rule as "insert cuts so each slice holds ~N cells of the header letter, right-to-left greedy" and finished at 26 %, saying "my best rule still misses the reference solver's habit of leaving one blank column at the start of a slice". The v4 demo showed a halved piece whose counted slice was on ONE side of the knife and whose other half lay alone in an uncounted slice - a picture that is equally consistent with "a half belongs to the slice on its left", the near-miss worth 56-60 %. v5 requires the two-sided picture instead: THE KNIFE GOES THROUGH A PIECE OF THE NAMED TOPPING AND BOTH NEIGHBOURING SLICES ARE COUNTED, each of them holding two only because of its half (a whole piece beside it). Whoever reads the demo with a one-sided convention counts one counted slice too few and can see, in the one picture he paid for, that his reading does not come to the digit. Measured on 272 cut demos: 100.0 % show the two-sided picture (v4: 0-77 % showed the one-sided one), 84.2 % show it with BOTH slices needing their half (the rest have one side needing it and the other holding two anyway), 96.7 % also show an uncounted slice with one lone WHOLE piece ("one is not enough"), and 6.6 % additionally show a slice of three. Rival readings that also come to the digit in a demo: a half counting only for its left slice 0.0 %, only for its right slice 0.0 %, halves ignored (pairs of whole pieces) 0.0 %, severed 0.0 %, slices touched 0.0 %, number of cuts 0.0 %, number of slices 0.0 %, two of any one topping 1.8 %, two pieces of anything 0.4 %. The one reading a demo cannot exclude is "slices holding three or more CELLS of the letter" (86.4 %): a slice holding two pieces holds three cells unless both are halves, so that reading is a near-synonym of the rule rather than a rival - it is worth 77 % against the scorer, and a player who reaches it has understood that the halves count.

HOW THE PICTURE IS BUILT. A 2-cell piece is halved only when the knife lands on the one column inside it, so a uniformly random cutting almost never carries the picture and it has to be constructed. pairb() picks a piece of the named topping, puts the cut through it, and then chooses the two neighbouring slice edges so that each side holds exactly one further piece of that topping and holds it WHOLE (it scans the ~15 columns either side for edges that give (2 pieces, 1 whole)), before filling the rest of the tray with random cuts, 4-8 slices in all. generate() draws 30 such cuttings per candidate topping and keeps a tray only if one of them carries the picture and also leaves an uncounted slice holding one whole piece; solve() draws from the same builder and prefers, in order: no structural rival reading coming to the digit (cuts, slices, severed, whole pairs, slices touched), the uncounted lone whole piece, no one-sided halves reading and no "two of any one topping" coming to the digit, both sides needing their half, and a slice of three.

WHY THE DIGIT IS NEVER 1. The two-sided picture needs two counted slices, so the caption cannot be 1 and generate() no longer looks for it. Measured over 20000 seeds the caption is 0 on 12.6 %, 2 on 25.8 % and 3 on 61.7 % of clues (3 dominates because generate() still publishes the RAREST count that survives its gates, and 3 is rarer than 2 on a random cutting). That is a slightly weaker checksum than v4's three-valued digit, and it is the price of the picture.

MEASURED WITNESS TABLE (500 fresh clues, seeds 100000-100499; a strategy "builds" an answer by searching up to 400 well-formed cuttings for one satisfying its own law, then is scored by the real scorer; "built" is how often such a cutting was found at all. The second column is the same strategy played by someone who has ALSO found the foothold: echo the clue when the caption says 0, apply the law otherwise. v4 measured on the same harness and seeds is in brackets.)

The payoff ladder is 0 % (no picture) -> 13 % (the format alone, from the nought clues) -> 18-28 % (well formed, no idea) -> 46-56 % (right measurement, wrong halves convention) -> 77-100 % (the whole insight, or a synonym of it). THE STRONGEST WRONG-HALVES CONVENTION IS "two or more, a half counting only for the slice on its left": 56.2 % on its own, 69.4 % with the foothold - and it is now the thing the demo exists to refute, which it does in 100 % of demos.

SHAPE AND JUNK ATTACKS on an otherwise correct answer (250 clues, 26 of them nought clues): reference 100 %; the caption line kept, crust rows removed, trailing spaces, blank lines inserted, leading/trailing blank lines - all 100 % (the scorer reads only lines containing ":", so the house rule about the parameter line is satisfied in both directions). All cuts removed 10.4 % and the clue itself 10.4 % - those are exactly the nought clues, where that IS the answer. A dough row deleted, duplicated or reordered, upper-cased, cheese turned to spaces, reversed left-right, one cut missing in one row, cuts shifted by one in one row - all 0.00 %. One extra cut through the middle of the widest slice: 43.2 % - that is not a witness (it needs a correct answer for that very clue) but a statement that the answer set is not a knife's edge.

SPEED AND SIZE (20000 seeds for generate, 300 for solve): generate mean 2.04 ms, median 1.56 ms, p99 7.7 ms, max 18.3 ms, no empty clue on 20000 seeds. solve mean 90 ms, median 51 ms, max 398 ms (cap 2000; it is paid only for a demo, and buys the two-sided picture). score mean 0.06 ms, max 4.1 ms on junk (cap 50). Sizes: scorer 448 chars (cap 512), solve 4960 (cap 5000), generate 8967, clue <= 205, solution <= 229. score(clue, solve(clue)) == 1 on 2000 further seeds and on every clue in the tables above. The nought costs nothing: generate() draws the flag first and builds the tray exactly as before.

HOW GENERATE CHOOSES THE DIGIT. For each tray and each topping with 5-7 pieces it takes 40 random well-formed cuttings, histograms the count, and keeps only counts that (i) are 2 or 3, (ii) occur on 2-15 of the 40 cuttings (5-37 % - rare enough that blind play is a foothold and not a coin flip, common enough that a player who has the rule finds a cutting in a few dozen tries), (iii) are not achieved by ANY equal-width cutting of that tray, at any number of slices and any rounding, and (iv) have a witness cutting carrying the demo picture. The rarest surviving count wins. Then, on 12 % of seeds, the digit published is 0 instead and the answer is the uncut tray.

INTENDED DISCOVERY PATH. (1) The caption says "slices" and the clue is the tray, so even a demo-less player sends the tray back with bars down it; that is well formed and scores ~9 % by accident. (2) The pool-wide "N verb" convention says to try the unchanged picture: it scores on every "0 slices" clue and on nothing else, which banks 13 % and confirms the format, the letter and the digit's meaning without a demo. (3) One demo confirms the cutting and shows a mushroom the knife went through with a counted slice on BOTH sides of it, each holding one whole mushroom and that half, beside a slice holding one whole mushroom that does not count. (4) The last step is the same as ever - that a halved piece belongs to both sides - but it is now on the picture rather than merely consistent with it: the one-sided reading counts one slice too few in the demo itself.

LEVERS IF IT DRIFTS. Too easy (the likely direction; the foothold lifts every wrong law by 13 points), in order of measured effect: (i) SIX toppings a row instead of five (18 pieces, the named one 7-9 of them) on a 30-36 tray - measured on v4, that alone took the halves-convention rows from 50/62/91 % to 32/37/15 %, at the price of generate 1.5 -> 3.2 ms and 0.4 % empty clues; (ii) drop the nought rate to 6 %; (iii) require the counted slice to hold nothing but that topping; (iv) narrow the rarity band to 2-8 of 40; (v) name two toppings and two digits as v2 did. Too hard: raise the nought rate; require BOTH sides of the halved piece to need their half in generate()'s gate as well as solve()'s preference (demo 84 % -> 100 %, generate ~2.0 -> ~2.6 ms); widen the rarity band, which raises the blind floor.
generate:
def place(r, W, letters):
    """One row of the tray: these toppings, two cells each, two cheese cells apart at
    least, in random positions, with a two-column crust at each end."""
    m = len(letters)
    cells = [":"] * W
    pcs = []
    for i, s in enumerate(sorted(r.sample(range(W + 2 - 3 * m), m))):
        j = s + 3 * i
        cells[j] = cells[j + 1] = letters[i]
        pcs.append((j + 2, letters[i]))
    return "##" + "".join(cells) + "##", pcs


def cutb(r, T, n):
    """A uniformly random cutting of a T-wide tray into n slices, each at least 3 wide."""
    if n < 2:
        return []
    b = []
    t = p = 0
    for x in sorted(r.sample(range(T - 2 * n - 1), n - 1)):
        t += x - p + 3
        p = x + 1
        b.append(t)
    return b


def side(P, x, lo, hi, T):
    """(pieces of x this slice holds, how many of them lie whole inside it)."""
    a = w = 0
    for c, L in P:
        if L == x and c + 1 >= lo and c < hi:
            a += 1
            w += c >= lo and c + 1 < hi
    return a, w


def pairb(r, P, X, T, x, nmax):
    """A cutting that carries THE picture this class lives on: the knife straight through
    a piece of x, and a WHOLE piece of x just inside the slice on each side, so both
    neighbours hold two - and each of them holds two only because of its half. Random
    cuts almost never do this (a 2-cell piece is halved only by the one column inside
    it), so the demo picture is built rather than waited for. None if it will not fit."""
    f = r.choice(X) + 1
    los = [lo for lo in range(max(0, f - 15), f - 2)
           if (lo == 0 or lo > 2) and side(P, x, lo, f, T) == (2, 1)]
    his = [hi for hi in range(f + 3, min(T, f + 16) + 1)
           if (hi == T or T - hi > 2) and side(P, x, f, hi, T) == (2, 1)]
    if not los or not his:
        return None
    lo = r.choice(los)
    hi = r.choice(his)
    m1, m2 = lo // 3, (T - hi) // 3
    opt = [(i, j) for i in range(min(m1, 5) + 1) for j in range(min(m2, 5) + 1)
           if 2 <= i + j <= min(6, nmax - 2)]
    if not opt:
        return None
    n1, n2 = r.choice(opt)
    return (cutb(r, lo, n1) + ([lo] if lo else []) + [f] + ([hi] if hi < T else [])
            + [hi + y for y in cutb(r, T - hi, n2)])


def eqb(T, n, m):
    """The three ways a tidy-minded player cuts a T-wide tray into n even slices."""
    if m == 2:
        return [(i * T + n // 2) // n for i in range(1, n)]
    q, e = T // n, T % n
    w = [q + (i < e if m else i >= n - e) for i in range(n)]
    b = []
    t = 0
    for v in w[:-1]:
        t += v
        b.append(t)
    return b


def sums(P, T, alpha):
    """Per letter: how many pieces start by column i, how many have ended by column i."""
    D = {}
    for L in alpha:
        D[L] = ([0] * (T + 4), [0] * (T + 4))
    for c, L in P:
        D[L][0][c] += 1
        D[L][1][c + 2] += 1
    for L in D:
        a, e = D[L]
        s = t = 0
        for i in range(T + 4):
            s += a[i]
            t += e[i]
            a[i] = s
            e[i] = t
    return D


def kof(a, e, b, T):
    """How many slices hold two or more pieces (a halved piece counts on both sides)."""
    lo = k = 0
    for hi in b:
        if a[hi - 1] - e[lo] > 1:
            k += 1
        lo = hi
    return k + (a[T - 1] - e[lo] > 1)


def cnt(D, L, b, T):
    """Pieces of L on each slice (a piece the knife went through counts on both sides)."""
    a, e = D[L]
    out = []
    lo = 0
    for hi in b + [T]:
        out.append(a[hi - 1] - e[lo])
        lo = hi
    return out


def whole(D, L, b, T):
    """Pieces of L lying entirely inside each slice."""
    a, e = D[L]
    out = []
    lo = 0
    for hi in b + [T]:
        out.append(e[hi] - (a[lo - 1] if lo else 0))
        lo = hi
    return out


def hand(b, T):
    """Are these slices visibly hand-cut - one of them narrow, and a wide spread
    between the widest and the thinnest - so that neatness is plainly not the rule?"""
    w = [q - p for p, q in zip([0] + b, b + [T])]
    return min(w) < 5 and max(w) - min(w) > 4


def pair(P, b, T, x, A, Wh):
    """THE picture, scored: a piece of x the knife halved with a COUNTED slice on both
    sides of the cut - so each half is plainly counted for its own side - and each of
    those slices holding two only because of its half (one whole piece beside it).
    2 = both sides are like that, 1 = one of them is, 0 = the picture is not there."""
    best = 0
    for c, L in P:
        if L != x:
            continue
        i = bisect.bisect_right(b, c)
        j = bisect.bisect_right(b, c + 1)
        if i == j or A[i] < 2 or A[j] < 2:
            continue
        best = max(best, (A[i] == 2 and Wh[i] == 1) + (A[j] == 2 and Wh[j] == 1))
    return best


def ok(D, P, b, T, x, A):
    """A cutting that can carry the demo this class lives on: hand-cut slices; a halved
    piece of x whose two halves are each counted for their side, at least one of those
    slices counting only because of its half; and SOME OTHER slice holding one WHOLE
    piece of x and not counted, so that "one is not enough" is on the picture too.
    solve() asks for more than this (both sides needing their half, a slice of three, no
    rival reading of the cut picture coming to k either)."""
    if not hand(b, T):
        return 0
    Wh = whole(D, x, b, T)
    if not pair(P, b, T, x, A, Wh):
        return 0
    return any(A[i] == 1 and Wh[i] == 1 for i in range(len(A)))


def hunt(D, P, T, x, pool):
    """The first cutting in pool that carries the demo picture this class lives on."""
    for b in pool:
        if ok(D, P, b, T, x, cnt(D, x, b, T)):
            return b
    return None


def generate(seed):
    r = random.Random(seed)
    nil = r.random() < 0.12                        # ~1 clue in 8 is "0 slices": the
    for _ in range(10):                            # answer is the tray left uncut
        W = r.randint(28, 34)                      # one tray size per batch, so the
        T = W + 4                                  # sampled cuttings are drawn once
        nmax = T // 3
        cuts = [cutb(r, T, r.randint(4, nmax)) for _ in range(40)]
        even = [eqb(T, n, m) for n in range(4, nmax + 1) for m in (0, 1, 2)]
        for _ in range(12):
            alpha = r.sample("mpotacsb", 3)
            bag = []                               # 15 toppings in fixed proportions, so
            for L, q in zip(alpha, r.choice(       # some topping always has 5-7 pieces
                    ((5, 5, 5), (6, 5, 4), (4, 5, 6), (7, 5, 3), (6, 6, 3), (4, 4, 7)))):
                bag += [L] * q
            r.shuffle(bag)
            rows = []
            P = []
            for i in range(3):
                row, pcs = place(r, W, bag[5 * i:5 * i + 5])
                rows.append(row)
                P += pcs
            cn = {}
            for c, L in P:
                cn[L] = cn.get(L, 0) + 1
            cand = [L for L in alpha if 5 <= cn.get(L, 0) <= 7]
            if not cand:
                continue
            r.shuffle(cand)
            D = sums(P, T, alpha)
            for x in cand:
                a, e = D[x]
                live = {2, 3}                      # the demo picture needs two counted
                for b in even:                     # slices, so 1 is not a caption here
                    live.discard(kof(a, e, b, T))  # equal slices must never be an answer
                    if not live:
                        break
                if not live:
                    continue
                hist = {}
                seen = {2: [], 3: []}
                for b in cuts:                     # how rare is each count on this tray?
                    k = kof(a, e, b, T)
                    hist[k] = hist.get(k, 0) + 1
                    if k in live:
                        seen[k].append(b)
                best = [k for k in live if 1 < hist.get(k, 0) < 16]
                if not best:
                    continue
                best.sort(key=lambda k: hist[k])           # the rarest count that works
                X = [c for c, L in P if L == x]
                for _ in range(30):                # built cuttings carrying the halved
                    b = pairb(r, P, X, T, x, nmax) # piece with a counted slice on each
                    if b:                          # side of the knife
                        k = kof(a, e, b, T)
                        if k in live:
                            seen[k].append(b)
                for k in best:
                    b = hunt(D, P, T, x, seen[k])
                    if b:
                        if nil:
                            k = 0
                        crust = "#" * T                         # the caption goes LAST,
                        return "%s\n%s\n%s\n%s %d slice%s" % (  # after the bottom crust
                            crust, "\n".join(rows), crust,      # row, as in every sibling
                            x, k, "s" * (k != 1))
    return ""
